findings.title: Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
findings.body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the leading prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany uses OR: [{method:SMS, scheduledDate<=now}, {retryCount:{gt:1}}]. The second branch has no method filter, so it matches EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminders as well as SMS. Only the SMS path increments retryCount today, but any non-SMS row that ever reaches retryCount 2 will be silently deleted, losing the reminder and suppressing the notification. Fix by adding method: SMS (and scheduled:false) to the retryCount branch.

findings.title: Retry count increment is not atomic
findings.body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts both failure paths do prisma.workflowReminder.update with data {retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1} using the value read earlier in findMany. Overlapping cron executions can read the same stale value and both write back the same incremented value, losing a count and allowing more retries than the intended limit of 2. Use atomic update {retryCount:{increment:1}} instead.

findings.title: Reminders with missing phone/message never increment retryCount
findings.body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the loop only updates the DB inside if (message?.length && message?.length>0 && sendTo). If sendTo is missing (e.g. no smsReminderNumber) or the rendered message is empty, the code does nothing: scheduled stays false and retryCount is unchanged. That same row is returned again by the unscheduledReminders query on every cron tick until scheduledDate ages out (up to 7 days), defeating the new 2-retry limit and causing unbounded reprocessing. The skip path must also bump retryCount or otherwise resolve the reminder.

findings.title: Failure-handler update can throw and prevent response
findings.body: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts the catch block does await prisma.workflowReminder.update to bump retryCount with no inner error handling. If that update itself fails (row just deleted by the leading deleteMany in a concurrent run, booking/step deleted, transient DB error, P2025 not-found), the exception escapes the handler, no HTTP response is sent, and the cron run fails. Wrap the cleanup update in its own try/catch or use updateMany and always return a response.
